title: Immediate Retry Storms and Unbounded Permanent-Failure Retries
pattern: A failing operation is retried immediately, overloading a dependency; in the stronger case, every error is retried indefinitely without distinguishing recoverable failures.
why_bad: Immediate retries against a failing or overloaded dependency act as a distributed denial-of-service attack from your own clients, amplifying load, preventing recovery, and triggering cascading meltdown of the downstream service [39:50, 13:107]. Indefinite retries of permanent failures such as bad credentials or malformed payloads additionally lock up the calling thread at 100% CPU and flood logs and disks without any path to success [7, Chapter 7, "Stubborn Link"].
detection: Case 36: a loop around a network, database, or other I/O call retries errors with no static or adaptive wait between attempts, including a bounded loop [13:107]. Case 395: a loop or recursion retries every `Err` indefinitely, without error classification (transient vs. permanent), backoff, or a maximum retry count. Do not require infinite retries for the first case, and do not treat a short bounded burst as meeting the second.
source: *Database Internals* (Petrov), Part II: Distributed Systems; *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (Adkins), Chapter 12 [39:50, 13:107]; *Alex Petrov - Database Internals*, Chapter 7 (Stubborn Link Retries) [7]
